correctness.rationale: The positive ODE has two distinct positive-rate exponentials with positive weights, because the characteristic polynomial is negative at D=b+e. The baseline three positive-time samples plus known zero-time initialization reconstruct the two decay roots and weight via a strictly positive Hankel variance. This identifies A1=a+theta1*d, D=b+e, B=ab. Holding D,B fixed, derivative of the Laplace water response with respect to A is minus the squared transform, so its time derivative is the strictly negative convolution -(W*W)(h); one positive-time second-condition water reading uniquely determines A2. The pair of A values yields d then a,b,e. Conversely the open interval z in (B/D,A1) parametrizes ALL positive first-condition alternatives with precisely identical complete water histories. Invariance of domain makes continuous injection of the open 4D positive parameter domain into fewer than four fixed scalar observations impossible, independently of sampling times or intervention choices. Reproducibility checker returned 2250 passing high-precision numerical assertions; analytic proof, not enumeration, establishes universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The mathematical object is a reversible aqueous/sediment tracer with independent loss in both pools, not an arbitrary parameter slice. Environmental eDNA data confound true molecular degradation with temporary sediment sequestration, as supported by Pont (2024), McKnight et al. (2024) and Sakata et al. (2020). The exact minimal 3+1 water-only design is useful before undertaking microcosm experiments: it shows the precise baseline obstruction and a sufficient selective experimental remedy without measuring sediment at any time. Complete all-positive-parameter fiber and minimal scalar count go beyond mere numerical inversion of a toy example. The scientific limitation is that interventions may alter several processes and small measurement noise may undermine numerical recovery; no field design efficacy is claimed.
